sectionsContent.title: Unit 5 Test · Written · Version C

concept.summary: Electronegativity (EN):  C 2.55 · O 3.44 · P 2.19 · S 2.58 · Cl 3.16 · Ge 2.01 · I 2.66

sectionsContent.directions: For each compound: add up the valence electrons and show the addition. Draw the Lewis structure with every lone pair. Name the shape. Find ΔEN for each different bond (higher EN − lower EN), then mark each bond PC (polar covalent) or NPC (nonpolar covalent). Then decide if the whole molecule is polar or nonpolar.

blocks.label: DRAW AND DECIDE (7 points per compound)
headers: ΔEN of each bond (show the subtraction) · 1

keyNotes: 7 points per compound, 28 total: valence e⁻ with the addition 1; Lewis structure 2 (1 right bonds incl. double bonds, 1 every lone pair with the total matching); shape 1; ΔEN 1; bond polarity 1; molecular polarity 1.
Slots: easy nonpolar (GeCl₄), lone pair on the center (PI₃), double bonds (OCS), three elements with carbon (CSCl₂).
Ge is in group 14 (4 valence e⁻), like C and Si. GeCl₄: polar bonds, symmetric, so nonpolar.
OCS: C in the center, O=C=S like CO₂. Linear, but the two ends pull differently (0.89 vs 0.03), so polar. Accept O–C≡S as a drawing (every atom still has 8); the shape and polarity are the same.
CSCl₂: put the double bond on S; Cl forms only one bond. If a student puts it on Cl, take off the drawing point only.
Accept the subtraction written either way round if the difference is right.
